author: lodekeeper
content:
Got the full picture from source. Here's the answer.

Lodestar has **two** builder circuit breakers, and which one is live depends on the fork — for a `buildoor` (Gloas/ePBS) devnet it's the second one.

**Pre-Gloas — missed-slot health gate** (`chain.ts::updateBuilderStatus`, runs every slot in `prepareNextSlot`):
- Signal is `forkChoice.getSlotsPresent(clockSlot - faultInspectionWindow)` = how many slots in the window actually had a block (not missed).
- Builder stays enabled only if `slotsPresent >= min(faultInspectionWindow - allowedFaults, clockSlot)`. Otherwise status flips to `BuilderStatus.circuitBreaker` and you build locally.
- Logic: too many missed slots ⇒ chain is unhealthy ⇒ don't hand block production to an external builder, self-build.

**Post-Gloas — EMPTY-block rate gate** (`chain/builderCircuitBreaker.ts`):
- In Gloas the proposer always produces the beacon block regardless of bid source, so missed *blocks* stop being a builder-health signal. Instead it counts canonical blocks that ended up **EMPTY** (payload not revealed) vs FULL, over the window (excluding the current slot since its payload status may be unresolved).
- Activates when `empty * faultInspectionWindow > allowedFaults * canonicalBlocks` — i.e. the EMPTY rate exceeds the fault budget, scaled by observed blocks so sparse windows still trip on a high EMPTY rate.
- Resumes selecting bids only when back within budget **and** it has seen ≥4 canonical blocks (`MIN_BLOCKS_TO_DEACTIVATE`) — a minimum recovery sample so it doesn't flap.

**Params** (`getFaultInspectionParams`, both share them):
- `faultInspectionWindow` default = `SLOTS_PER_EPOCH + rand(0..SLOTS_PER_EPOCH)` (≈32–63 slots), min `SLOTS_PER_EPOCH`. Randomized so validators don't all flip in lockstep.
- `allowedFaults` default = `min(configured, floor(faultInspectionWindow/4))` → ~25% budget.

author: lodekeeper
content:
- CLI: `--builder.faultInspectionWindow`, `--builder.allowedFaults`.

This is a **chain-health override** and is orthogonal to `--builder.selection` (maxprofit/builderalways/…) and the per-block `shouldOverrideBuilder` EL signal — when the breaker is active it forces local build regardless of selection.

author: potuz
content:
The only reason I am hearing from Pari/Barnabas to fallback to self-building: 

- Because it takes away one item from testing and it makes it easier to diagnose.  

This may seem true on first sight but it is actually false: a bug in the CL may make payloads disappear, just as a bug on the builder would. But it can also create all sorts of other bugs that a builder could not.  Diagnosing block building paths on the local build path is harder than on the external builder: failure to deliver from the builder and we do not care if it was it's CL or its EL, we simply cut it off... failure from delivering a self built payload and we have no clue what failed, it could be the CL, the EL, a combination, etc.. and we NEED to diagnose it to fix the chain. 

Arguments to not fall back to self-building:

- The chain is more reliable with many builders instead of 1, one active non-blacklisted builder will keep the chain running, that's 1 of N instead of 1/1. 
- The chain can advance even if all ELs from all active validators are failing to build blocks, there are plenty of scenarios that can trigger this: a failure to identify limits for example can lead to block building time to take more than the timeout, forcing clients to censor, we've had this already when we talked about gas limits and deposits. Builders can change this, local builders cannot. 
- Local builders that are stressed can't propagate blocks correctly or at least have a much harder time than external builders.
